ruleset.name: YouNeedMe
ruleset.description:
Baseline PMD ruleset for YouNeedMe. Wired as non-blocking (isIgnoreFailures = true in build.gradle.kts) so findings are tracked in CI without gating the build day one.
The exclusions below were reviewed one by one against real occurrences in this codebase (never bulk-disabled) and fall into two groups: - Rules that fire on patterns Bukkit/JDBC/Mongo/this project's conventions require, so every occurrence was a false positive (AssignmentInOperand: idiomatic ps.setX(i++, value) JDBC binding; LooseCoupling: org.bson.Document is the Mongo driver's own type, not a project choice; UseVarargs/AvoidFieldNameMatchingMethodName: would fight the Bukkit CommandExecutor/TabCompleter override shape and this codebase's field-plus-same-named-accessor convention; AvoidCatchingGenericException: deliberate defensive boundary catches, e.g. YnmCommand#onCommand so one broken subcommand can't dump a stack trace into a player's chat; AvoidInstantiatingObjectsInLoops: normal per-slot ItemStack construction in GUIs; UseConcurrentHashMap/UseProperClassLoader: would be wrong here - main-thread-confined caches and anchor.getClass().getClassLoader() is the correct way to load a plugin's own bundled resources; AvoidLiteralsInIfCondition/ AvoidDuplicateLiterals: inline slot indices, arg-length checks and lang keys are this codebase's convention throughout; AvoidUsingVolatile: single-writer flag/reference fields, the textbook-correct use of volatile, not a compound read-modify-write; ExhaustiveSwitchHasDefault/AvoidReassigningParameters/AvoidBranchingStatementAsLastInLoop: an explicit default is kept deliberately (checkstyle's MissingSwitchDefault guards against a future enum constant silently falling through), the JDBC index-counter parameter is the same idiom as AssignmentInOperand, and a retry loop's early `return` on success alongside `continue` on failure is normal control flow, not a dead loop). - Size/complexity metrics (GodClass, CognitiveComplexity, CouplingBetweenObjects, ExcessiveImports, TooManyFields, ExcessivePublicCount, DataClass, NPathComplexity, SwitchDensity, AvoidDeeplyNestedIfStmts) that flag already-working, tested classes (Services, JsonStorage, MongoStorage, ShopEditorGui, TradeGui, KitEditorGui, AhGui, PlayerShopListener, LanguageManager, VaultEconomyProvider) which would need deep structural refactors to satisfy - tracked as a known follow-up, not silently ignored. - The two JUnit style rules (UnitTestContainsTooManyAsserts, UnitTestAssertionsShouldIncludeMessage) conflict with this test suite's established style of several related assertions per test without messages. Every other finding PMD reports is expected to be a real, fixable issue.
